source.prompt:
Create six new original high-quality full-body transparent solo cutouts for these TWO specific referenced game characters as they appear in three incompatible narratives of the House of Atreus. First attached ref gives Electra's face and body, second gives her brother Orestes's face and body. Third gives Electra's related look at the jury scene, reference only. Preserve both EXACT recognizable characters with unchanged face shapes, nose, brow, apparent age, proportion, warm olive complexions, eyes and dark hair. They can be recognized as siblings but keep the specific different faces they have. Keep Electra's short dark cropped hair, distinct narrow nose, quiet intense eye, slender long limbs. Keep Orestes's black curly silhouette, straight jaw, pensive eye and slim strong legs. NO generic face substitutions. All six appearances change posture, drape and materials for the scene. Original naturalistic hand-painted MATTE OIL realism like the references, matte worn folds, ancient Greek shapes, restrained mineral palette. No letters, text, layout marks, titles, plates, frames, borders, props, shadows, or background. True RGBA transparency outside bodies.

Exact square image, mathematical 3 columns and 2 rows, identical-sized rectangular 2:3 cells. One wholly self-contained person per cell, complete head and both feet within its cell, generous transparent gutters and 9% air above head and below feet. Center the figure within its cell with safe margin left and right. Never overlap, no panorama. All full-body figures, individually distinct stances, in three-quarter view, oriented slightly left wherever natural. Color and shape are visible from face to torso even in a tiny thumbnail. Keep head side profile clean enough for future card crop.

Top row all ELECTRA, in this exact left to right order: 
1. Aeschylus tomb mourner. Long layered coal-black shawl peaks to one shoulder and angles across her claret undertunic. A flat rough red strip sits high across chest. She inclines her head gently and draws one forearm inward to her sternum, the other arm relaxed. Dark mourning silhouette and intact sandals. Hair visible.
2. Sophocles Mycenae palace threshold. Narrow soot-brown full skirt and a PARCHMENT-CREAM wool mantle that sits sharply over both shoulders, a single narrow faded madder vertical edge. Upright confrontational stance, chin set, holds one loose mantle fold high by collarbone. Formal straight arm, no jewelry, same young Electra with short black hair. A pale tall shoulder square to distinguish the palace look.
3. Euripides Argive farmhouse. Worn cropped umber work wrap over gray-olive rough linen, faded MADDER waist sash and clay-red narrow edge visible at neckline, sleeves tied back at shoulders and strong square elbow. No palace refinement. Slight tilt as she finishes work, one bare forearm resting across waist and the other hand at hip. Same Electra short hair and face, lean and practical, ankle-length skirt remains complete.

Bottom row all ORESTES, in this exact left to right order:
4. Aeschylus tomb traveler, with dark olive tunic, charcoal-brown traveler wrap folded into a tall diagonal sloping to right shoulder, tiny old bronze clasp, and one hand gently open below waist. No sword, no staff. Both legs and sandals fully visible. Same dark curly clean-shaven young face as reference.
5. Sophocles Mycenae arrival. Wear a sharply folded muted SLATE BLUE short travel cloak over a pale flax tunic, high seam near neck, lean guarded stance and spare cloth at elbow. Opposite hand gathers cloak at mid-rib. A tighter cloak and cooler silhouette to distinguish this palace arrival. Same dark curls, no hat, same smooth young face.
6. Euripides Argive farmhouse visitor. Low loosely draped TOBACCO OCHRE, weathered half cloak on one shoulder over a cool desaturated olive tunic, cloth pin at left shoulder, sun-faded weather marks at knees. He crouches slightly into a conversational, empty-handed pose, looking toward the farmer's door. Same young Orestes face and visible curly hair. Show complete legs and sandals with margin.

Maintain six clear spots, exact cell order, nominal torso and head heights consistent within each person row. Wide gutters, headroom, full sandal room. Transparent stage sprite atlas for production slicing. No stylized icons, anime, acrylic covers, or studio backdrop.

assets.name: The Argolid Crossroads
assets.prompt: Create a TWO-PANEL production contact sheet of original landscape painting assets for a Greek drama game. Final image format SQUARE 1:1. STACK exactly two full bleed panoramic landscapes vertically: one complete landscape in TOP half of canvas and the different other one in BOTTOM half. Both panels equal height, full width edge to edge. The ONLY seam is a perfectly horizontal solid hot-magenta (#ff00ff) separator line through center, from edge to edge. No margins of any kind, external frames, logos, titles, type, other marks or lettering. No vertical seams, no additional panels. Finish both separately in naturalistic fine matte oil-paint textures, like the authentic architectural and landscape art in the two left panels of the supplied Delphi style reference (no copying its layout or characters). Period believable material textures. Each design has its strongest landmark at the center (x 50 percent and y about 40 percent of its own panel), so it reads when just the central quarter of the width is cropped for portrait. Keep the whole broad natural bottom third in each picture empty quiet visibly walkable ground, a stage apron for separately placed figures. View at consistent eye height. Elevation expressed above the foreground. NO people, figures, animals, lettering, fantasy effects, game interface or map iconography. Entirely opaque. TOP location is The Argolid Crossroads. Wide red-brown Argolid foothill cart track fanning out in a clean three-way Y. A weathered gray narrow route stele and low split dry-stone wall catch side light at the center of the fork, with no legible inscription. A well-worn right fork falls toward a distant sea sliver and dry reeds. A dry gravel left branch rises into hill country behind a half-wild olive terrace. A few late poppies far in the roadside grass, cinnamon dust and warm late afternoon, nondescript uneven olive hills. The stone and the division in the tracks must define this specific place. BOTTOM location is Delphic Temple. Delphic public approach and exterior threshold in Greece, a proper modest broad-fronted ancient temple on the steep northern slope of Delphi, with worn buff limestone Doric columns and an especially legible upright dark doorway visible through the pair of columns across the central quarter of the image. In the wings transparent blue-lavender mountain cliffs and lower retaining terraces, faded terracotta acroterion off one wing, silver laurel. Crisp early sunlight on worn stone and enough shadow to make the centered doorway readable. The broad forecourt is the public crossroads linking uphill Oeta, the road to Athens and the narrow side terrace that runs to Apollo's court. Do not show a tripod. This scene is in the same geological setting as the Delphi reference but the main place here is the exterior temple with the columns and doorway as main landmark. Two full-bleed wide independent environments, perfectly horizontal divider.
